The concept of the Memorial Temple emerged as a tribute to Freemasons who lost their lives during World War I, replacing an earlier Masonic Temple situated in a mixed-use building on Dorchester Street since 1895.

Officially dedicated and opened on February 12, 1930, this historic masonic temple was recognized as a National Historic Site of Canada in 2001, celebrated for its elegant Beaux-Arts architecture. The concept of the Memorial Temple emerged as a tribute to Freemasons who lost their lives during World War I, replacing an earlier Masonic Temple situated in a mixed-use building on Dorchester Street since 1895.

The Grand Lodge of Quebec convened for the first time in the Memorial Temple on February 12, 1930, during its 60th Annual Communication. The temple honors not only those who perished in World War I but also those who died in World War II and the Korean War.
